pattern.crimePattern: the enforcer "Fundi" kills the fisherman who saw him dump a witness's body, wearing a fake limp so witnesses remember the limp and not the man
pattern.notes: Fictional garage, newspaper and phone line. The fake limp is a costume built to be remembered; the one genuinely disabled character, Abiud, is suspected by the village and explicitly cleared by the evidence, and is the witness who looked at the face. Tom Ochieng is the case-10 courier.

ob.text: The chairman of Usoma Beach Management Unit reports a fisherman, Walter Ogada (63), found dead in the water hyacinth beside his boat at Usoma beach at 06:50.

facts.text: Walter Ogada was found dead in the water hyacinth beside his boat at Usoma beach at 06:50.
Walter lay face down in the hyacinth beside his boat. Three small wounds on his shoulder.
Walter's statement, 15 January: on 4–5 January at about 02:00, near the hyacinth mat, a white motorboat with a blue stripe; a man dropped a bundle tied with stones. "He limped badly."
Dr. Chebii, 16 January: the body that surfaced on 15 January is Tom Ochieng, 29, courier. Dead before entering the water; struck; weighted with stones on blue nylon rope.
Tom's notebook, last page: "If anything happens to me: Fundi — Kibos Motors."
Consolata: "Tom said Fundi was two men: one who collects and one who works."
Consolata: Tom was out on bail from November and had started telling his lawyer about "Fundi".
Taifa Daily, 24 January: "Usoma fisherman Walter Ogada says he saw a body dumped."
Livingstone: on 25 January a man phoned "from a fish company" and asked where Walter keeps his boat. "I told him. I thought he wanted to buy fish."
Livingstone was at home in Usoma village with his family from 21:00.
Mary: at 22:25 Walter said a buyer was bringing cash to the boat at 22:45 and went down. He never came back. She adds that Alloys Ondeng' once accused him of stealing nets.
Walter's phone: a call on 26 January at 22:20 from 07xx xxx 773, saved as "Mnunuzi" (buyer). WhatsApp: "Meet at your boat 22:45, cash."
Walter's phone and KSh 3,800 were still under the bow seat of his boat.
Records: 07xx xxx 773 is registered to the national ID of a man who died nine years ago.
Records, 07xx xxx 773: Kibos 21:00–22:00; Airport Road 22:05–22:15; Usoma 22:35–23:20. It also called Livingstone on 25 January.
Fuel station video, Airport Road, 22:08–22:12: Benedict Mbuvi gets out of a grey Kibos Motors station wagon and walks normally to the till and back.
Abiud: at about 22:40 a man limping heavily walked from a car to the boats. At about 23:00 he heard splashing.
Abiud's radio check-ins to the security company are logged from the guard hut at 22:45 and 23:15.
Boot prints in the wet sand by Walter's boat: the right ordinary, the left deeper with a square-edged heel mark.
There are no crutch marks anywhere in the wet sand.
Records, Benedict's own line: exactly the same masts as 07xx xxx 773, minute for minute, 21:00–23:20. The two phones travelled together.
Kibos Motors alarm: armed at 21:30, disarmed at 06:50. Nobody was inside the garage all night.
In the Kibos Motors yard: a white motorboat with a blue stripe, on a trailer.
In the yard: a reel of blue nylon rope.
In Benedict's car boot: a left boot with a 3 cm wooden block glued inside the heel.
In the car boot: a three-pronged grapnel anchor with hyacinth fibres in its prongs.
Kibos Motors job book: Walter Ogada was never a customer.
Kibos Motors cash book: "M.H. — collection", every month.
Photo line-up: Daniel Gichuru, Calvin Wamalwa and Millicent Akoth each point to Benedict. "That's Fundi." Gichuru adds: "But he limped. Badly."
Abiud at the line-up: "Everyone looks at my leg. I look at faces." That face, under the beach light, walking to the boats at 22:40.
Bar tab: Alloys and four friends, opened 20:30, closed 00:40.
BMU minutes: the net dispute between Alloys and Walter was settled by the committee on 20 January.
BMU minutes: no levy dispute with Walter in eleven years.
Mwende: Kioko slept at her house in Kibos on Monday night, from 19:00.
Autopsy: three puncture wounds in a triangular pattern, as from a three-pronged grapnel, then drowning: he was held under.
Autopsy: death between 22:45 and 23:30.
Autopsy: no bite, no propeller cuts, a sound heart.
Comparison: the left prints by Walter's boat were made by the blocked boot, square heel edge and all.
Lab: hyacinth fibres and Walter's blood on the grapnel's prongs.
Lab: the rope on the garage reel and the rope that bound Tom's body are the same: colour, weave and fibre count.
Benedict: "I was at my garage until midnight, then home. I've never been to Usoma."
Benedict: "I don't own a boat."
Benedict, shown the line-up: "You keep looking for a man. Kivuli is a desk." Then he asks for a lawyer.
Kioko: "Fundi was in the garage all night. I was there."
Kioko: he wasn't at the garage; he sleeps at his mother's. "He told me to say it. If anyone asks, he was at the garage."
Alloys: "I was drinking in town."
Alloys: "We settled it. Walter even bought the first round."
Abiud: "Everyone's saying 'the limping man'. Look at me. You think I could hold a man under water?"
Livingstone: "I told a caller where his boat was."

proof.concludes: Walter saw a body dumped from a white motorboat with a blue stripe on 5 January. It was Tom Ochieng, out on bail and talking, who had written: "If anything happens to me: Fundi — Kibos Motors."
After the newspaper named him, a caller on a dead man's ID found out where Walter kept his boat and lured him there at 22:45. That phone moved Kibos, Airport Road, Usoma.
Benedict's own phone moved with the caller's minute for minute, and at 22:10 the fuel-station camera shows him walking normally.

The man at the boats limped, but the prints have a square block in the left heel, and that boot is in Benedict's car. The limp is a costume. Abiud, checking in from his hut, leaves no crutch marks. Walter died between 22:45 and 23:30.

Benedict wasn't at his garage; his apprentice lied for him. His grapnel carries Walter's blood, his rope bound Tom, and four witnesses know his face. Benedict Mbuvi struck Walter with a grapnel and held him under the hyacinth because Walter had seen him dump Tom Ochieng's body and gone public.
The body Walter saw dumped was Tom Ochieng, the Haraka courier who collected the Mvua order on River Road in case 10.

eliminations.why: Kioko slept at his mother's in Kibos. His crime is the lie he was told to tell.
Alloys was on a bar tab in town from 20:30 to 00:40.

Abiud was at the beach, in his hut, checking in at 22:45 and 23:15. The prints by the boat were made by a blocked boot, and there are no crutch marks anywhere in the sand. The man the village suspected is the one who looked at the killer's face.
Livingstone was at home with his family from 21:00. He was deceived, not involved.
A triangle of punctures, not a bite.
A sound heart; he was wounded and held under.
The net quarrel was settled on 20 January, and Alloys was in town.
No levy dispute in eleven years.
Walter was never a Kibos Motors customer.
His cash and phone were still in the boat.
Gichuru is alive and in custody; he picked Fundi out of the line-up.
Calvin is alive and in custody; he picked Fundi out of the line-up.
Hezekiah's body was found and named in October. The January report names Tom Ochieng.
That pin is a note, not a body.

reconstruction.text: Benedict Mbuvi is Fundi: Mvua's collector. When he collects or threatens, he wears a left boot with a wooden block in the heel and limps, so every witness remembers the limp and nobody remembers a mechanic who walks perfectly well.

Tom Ochieng, out on bail, starts telling his lawyer about Fundi. On the night of 4–5 January Benedict kills him and drops him by the hyacinth mat from his white-and-blue motorboat. Walter, checking his nets, sees a limping man heave a bundle over the side.
15 January: the body surfaces and Walter makes his statement. 24 January: the newspaper names him. 25 January: a "fish buyer" asks Livingstone where Walter keeps his boat.

26 January, 22:10. Benedict stops for fuel and walks to the till like any man, forgetting the cameras. At Usoma he puts on the boot. At the boats he strikes Walter with a grapnel and holds him under the hyacinth.
His apprentice says the boss was at the garage all night. Abiud, on his crutch at the hut door, had watched the limping man walk past the beach light, and had looked at his face.

afterVerdict.beat: Benedict's one sentence, shown the line-up, is pinned to t_kivuli: "You keep looking for a man. Kivuli is a desk."

Pattern File: Fundi's thread gets a face, Benedict's custody photograph, and closes as IDENTIFIED. A new pin on t_registry: the caller's phone was registered to the ID of a man nine years dead, the same trick as the ghost members in case 37.
Mwalimu's voice-note, the first in weeks: "A desk. Write that down. Then burn the note."
Amani's notebook, in the margin beside the boot photograph: "Everyone remembered the limp. Nobody remembered the man."
Collectible: Walter's carved wooden fishing float, given to Amani by Mary Ogada: "He said you'd come. He said someone always comes in the end."

clockPlan.note: Three stamps, the region maximum: records on the caller, records on Benedict, the warrant on the garage. Detain Benedict after the search; the trace (12 h) and rope (8 h) results and the line-up come back inside his 24 hours. No rush.
